programs.name: suacor
programs.purpose: Compute the autocorrelation of each input trace.

params.name: ntout
params.description: Number of output samples; the selfdoc says it should be odd.

params.name: norm
params.description: If nonzero, divide the output by the zero-lag value, unless that value is zero.

params.name: sym
params.description: If nonzero, start the output at lag -(ntout-1)/2 using integer arithmetic; otherwise start at zero lag.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Correlation uses floating-point accumulation; normalization divides by the computed zero-lag value. f1 is set to -dt*ntout/2 even when sym=0.
programs.difficulty_reason: It correlates each trace and optionally normalizes the result.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suacor ntout=31 norm=1 sym=1
suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suacor ntout=24 norm=0 sym=0

programs.name: suacorfrac
programs.purpose: Apply a fractional autocorrelation or autoconvolution operation in the frequency domain.

params.name: a
params.description: Exponent applied to the complex amplitude.

params.name: b
params.description: Multiplier applied to the complex phase.

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: from first trace header dt for seismic data or d1 otherwise
params.description: Listed in the selfdoc, but the program does not read a dt parameter; it requires the selected header value to be nonzero.

params.name: verbose
params.description: If nonzero, report whether the first trace is seismic.

params.name: ntout
params.default: computed: from first trace header ns
params.description: Read but never used to change the output length.

params.name: sym
params.description: If nonzero, negate odd frequency bins before the inverse transform.

params.name: power
params.description: Appears in the selfdoc usage line, but the program does not read or use it; its type is not specified in the source.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The PFA FFT and inverse FFT are unnormalized, so even a=b=0 scales samples by nfft. Complex powers use float intermediates with exp, log, atan2, cos and sin, whose results can vary by platform. When a=0, dopow returns 1 regardless of b. The program copies only the original nt samples back and ignores ntout.
programs.difficulty_reason: It applies complex frequency-domain powers using forward and inverse FFTs.

test_cases.description: Default power operation with advisory output.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suacorfrac a=0 b=0 verbose=1

test_cases.description: Fractional operation with symmetric frequency shift.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suacorfrac a=0.5 b=0.5 sym=1 ntout=63
suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suacorfrac a=1 b=-1 sym=0

programs.license_note: Credits UHouston's Chris Liner; based on Hale's crpow.

programs.name: suconv
programs.purpose: Convolve each input trace with a supplied numeric filter or SU trace.

params.name: sufile
params.description: SU filter file; either sufile or filter is required, and sufile takes precedence.

params.name: filter
params.description: Filter coefficients; required if sufile is absent.

params.name: panel
params.description: With sufile, 0 uses its first trace for every input trace; 1 reads one filter trace per input trace.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Convolution uses floating-point accumulation. In panel=1 the return value of fgettr is ignored, so a short filter file can reuse stale trace data; the allocated filter is also replaced without being freed.
programs.difficulty_reason: It reads a filter and performs direct per-trace convolution.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suconv filter=1,2,1 panel=0

test_cases.description: Use one SU filter trace for all input traces.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=32 ntr=1 > in.su && suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suconv sufile=in.su panel=0
suplane nt=32 ntr=4 > in.su && suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suconv sufile=in.su panel=1

programs.name: surefcon
programs.purpose: Convolve forward and reverse shot traces with a specified trace offset.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUREFCON -  Convolution of user-supplied Forward and Reverse

params.name: sufile
params.description: SU file containing the offset forward-shot traces.

params.name: xy
params.description: Number of initial file traces to skip; must be nonnegative. The selfdoc labels it required, but the code defaults it to zero.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Convolution uses floating-point accumulation. Input and filter lengths are taken from their first selected traces and reused for subsequent traces; output dt is integer-divided by two.
programs.difficulty_reason: It pairs two streams at a trace offset and directly convolves each pair.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=4 > in.su && suplane nt=64 ntr=4 | surefcon sufile=in.su xy=0
suplane nt=64 ntr=5 > in.su && suplane nt=64 ntr=4 | surefcon sufile=in.su xy=1

programs.license_note: Credits UNSW's D. Palmer and K.T. Lee and says the program is based on suconv; cites Palmer's refraction convolution work.

programs.name: suxcor
programs.purpose: Cross-correlate input traces with a numeric filter or corresponding SU traces.

params.name: sufile
params.description: SU filter file; either sufile or filter is required, and sufile takes precedence. Required for a valid panel=1 run.

params.name: filter
params.description: Filter coefficients; required if sufile is absent.

params.name: vibroseis
params.description: If positive, use this output length, start at zero lag, and set output delrt to zero.

params.name: first
params.description: If nonzero, use the supplied filter as the first correlation input; otherwise use it as the second.

params.name: panel
params.description: If 1, use corresponding traces from sufile and apply the specified window.

params.name: ftwin
params.description: Starting window offset used with panel=1.

params.name: ltwin
params.description: Ending window offset used to calculate the integer window step with panel=1.

params.name: ntwin
params.default: computed: from first input trace header ns
params.description: Window length for panel=1; otherwise reset to the input trace length.

params.name: ntrc
params.description: Number of traces per gather for resetting the panel window position.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Correlation uses floating-point accumulation. Panel window slope uses integer division and starts at ftwin plus one step on the first trace. Panel=1 with filter= and no sufile passes a null file pointer to fgettr; window bounds and ntrc are not validated.
programs.difficulty_reason: It supports per-trace filter files, alternate correlation orders, vibroseis output, and a moving panel window.

test_cases.description: Correlate with an explicit filter in the default order.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suxcor filter=1,2,1 first=1 panel=0

test_cases.description: Use an SU filter with reversed correlation order and vibroseis output.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=32 ntr=1 > in.su && suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suxcor sufile=in.su first=0 vibroseis=64

test_cases.description: Correlate corresponding traces with a sloping window.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=4 > in.su && suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suxcor sufile=in.su panel=1 ftwin=2 ltwin=10 ntwin=64 ntrc=4 first=1

programs.license_note: Credits UTK's Rick Williams for the vibroseis correlation option.
